name: hacker-background

frames.best_why: Green columns fill the whole panel top to bottom, showing the falling-code effect at full strength.

tagline: Green characters stream down a black screen like falling code.
summary: A canvas of bright green letters raining down in narrow columns over black, each column leaving a fading tail. It fills its area and sits behind whatever text you layer on top.
appearance: A black surface covered in thin vertical columns of small monospaced green characters. The brightest letter sits at the head of each column and the characters above it dim into a greyer trail, so the rain looks denser near the top and sparse towards the bottom.
behaviour: Random letters fall column by column at roughly thirty frames a second, each pass painting a faint dark wash that slowly wipes away the tails. When a column reaches the bottom it restarts at the top at a random moment, so the pattern never repeats.
demo_content: Centred mono caption "Access granted" above a white heading reading "Wake up, Neo."
search_phrases: green letters falling like the matrix
animated code rain behind a hero
use_when: A page needs an instant hacker or cyberpunk mood behind a short headline.
avoid_when: Green on black fights light themes, and the constant motion distracts from long text.
customise: Colour, font size and fall speed are props; the character set and the fade strength are written into the canvas loop.
weight_why: A full-canvas 2D text redraw about thirty times a second, constant but cheap per frame.

a11y.note: The canvas is purely decorative yet has no aria-hidden and no reduced-motion check, so the rain never stops.

issues: The canvas is measured from the window, not its container, so in a short box the rain can overflow or stop short.
polish_why: A clean, familiar matrix-rain effect with correct trails; nothing beyond the well-known pattern.
title: Hacker Background
